transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Asha (CTO - Nyla), Liam (Lead Infra), Priya (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Nyla is evaluating a Private / VPC deployment of Redwood for PHI workflows. Primary concerns: VPC peering vs private endpoints, CIDR overlap, egress patterns, KMS/integration for key management and audit logs, region constraints for latency and data residency. They want an architecture doc and to schedule a network deep-dive next week.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick us off. Um, quick intros — I'm Maya Thompson, AE at Redwood. Diego is our systems engineer, he'll cover the networking bits.
[00:08] Asha: Hi, I'm Asha, CTO at Nyla Medical. We have Liam — hey Liam — and Priya on for security. Thanks for making time.
[00:15] Liam: Hey, thanks.
[00:17] Priya: Hi all.
[00:19] Diego: Great, quick agenda — high level ask, current infra, networking constraints, then we'll go into peering/endpoint options and security questions. Sound good?
[00:27] Asha: Yep. So context: we're building clinical document summarization and triage models, PHI in scope. We're debating hosted vs dedicated vs private. Hosted is attractive cost-wise but compliance and residency lean toward Private in our VPC.
[00:41] Maya: Totally understood. For Private we provide a customer VPC deployment model where the control plane can be managed (we can do a private control plane) and the inference nodes run in your VPC or peered. Diego, do you want to cover the connectivity patterns?
[00:53] Diego: Sure. There are two main approaches: VPC peering / Transit gateway to connect Redwood-managed subnets into your network, or Private Endpoints (we call them private-apis or private endpoints) that sit behind AWS PrivateLink. Each has tradeoffs.
[01:07] Liam: Can you expand on the tradeoffs? Particularly we have fairly strict egress rules and a shared NAT gateway with limited bandwidth.
[01:13] Diego: Yeah; with VPC peering — or TGW — our inference hosts would be in a Redwood-controlled account and peered into yours. That gives low-latency, direct routing, easier for large data flows. But you need to ensure CIDR ranges don't overlap and manage route tables. With PrivateLink, you get an endpoint in your account and traffic goes over the AWS backbone to our service, which is simpler for security but can add a small latency and you pay for endpoint hours and data processing. PrivateLink also avoids route table changes.
[01:41] Priya: For PHI, auditability is huge. Do you support customer-managed KMS and bring-your-own-key?
[01:47] Maya: Yes, we support KMS integration for encryption-at-rest, and in Private deployments we can integrate with your KMS via cross-account grants. Diego: to add, audit logs — we surface request logs and model usage events to your logging endpoint; we can push to a customer S3 bucket or to a SIEM over a private connection.
[02:03] Liam: Ok, what about outbound egress to third-party endpoints? Our security posture says no public internet egress except through our proxy — will Redwood respect that?
[02:12] Diego: In Private mode we can keep inference traffic inside your VPC; any model downloads or repo pulls during provisioning can be done via an outbound NAT that you control, or we can pre-stage model artifacts in your S3 bucket. For runtime calls we don't require public egress if you use the VPC peering/transit route. If you use PrivateLink there's still traffic to our infra but it's over AWS backbone, not public internet.
[02:36] Asha: Good. Region constraints: we need processing to happen in us-east-1 for data residency and latency to our services. Can Redwood place inference nodes in specific AZs/regions?
[02:45] Maya: Yes — Private deployments allow you to pin region and AZs. For Dedicated we also support region pinning. We usually recommend colocating in the same region for sub-50ms intra-region performance.
[02:55] Liam: Sub-50 sounds promising. We'll want to run a baseline with our typical payload sizes (docs ~3–5KB, batch sizes variable). Can you do a quick perf test once network is set up?
[03:06] Diego: Absolutely. Once networking is connected we can run a latency/cost baseline. We'll need an example workload and maybe access to a test VPC or peered connectivity.
[03:14] Priya: About identity — SSO and RBAC. We use Okta and SCIM. How do you integrate?
[03:19] Maya: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user management. For service-to-service auth you can use mTLS or private endpoints with IAM policies; we can align with your security team's preferences.
[03:30] Asha: How long does provisioning a Private deployment usually take?
[03:33] Maya: Typical timeline is 4–8 weeks depending on approvals and network readiness. If the VPC side is ready and there's no CIDR overlap it's closer to four. If we need on-prem or air-gapped options, it takes longer.
[03:44] Liam: One concern: our CIDR ranges are pretty congested; we're running corporate 10.0.0.0/8 shaped into a few /16s. We might not be able to allocate clean ranges for peering. Does Redwood support routing via TGW attachments and overlapping CIDR with NAT translation?
[03:59] Diego: We don't recommend overlapping CIDR; TGW doesn't magically resolve overlapping ranges. Options: use PrivateLink, which avoids peering and route changes, or use a transit setup with NATing at the VPC edge — but NAT introduces complexity and can impact source IPs. Another pattern is to host the inference nodes in a dedicated VPC inside your account to avoid peering overlap — we can support deploying into your account if that's preferred.
[04:26] Priya: Deploying into our account would be ideal for auditability. What permissions do you require?
[04:31] Diego: Minimal IAM role with CloudFormation permission to create the required infra or we provide a CloudFormation / Terraform template for you to run. We typically need VPC/subnet IDs, route table updates (if peering), Security Group guidelines, and KMS grants if you want BYOK.
[04:44] Asha: Hmm ok. On compliance — can you share SOC2 and penetration test reports?
[04:48] Maya: Yes, we'll share our SOC 2 report and ISO docs under NDA. We also have a pen-test summary. I'll attach these to the thread.
[04:56] Priya: Are there limits on concurrent requests and throughput on Private vs Dedicated?
[05:01] Diego: Dedicated gives predictable throughput with reserved GPU pools. Private can be either — if we deploy in your account we can size a dedicated pool for you; otherwise, Private with shared capacity might have burst limits. We'll propose sizing based on your QPS and latency targets.
[05:16] Liam: Cost — is there a large delta between Dedicated reserved capacity and Private in our account?
[05:21] Maya: If it's in your account, cost is mostly infra plus our platform fee. Dedicated reserved capacity bundles infra, support, and SLAs. We'll provide a detailed comparison in the pricing doc — I'll include some example TCO.
[05:33] Asha: For the next steps — we want: architecture doc, network deep-dive scheduled, and preliminary pricing. Also need instructions for capturing VPC info.
[05:42] Maya: Agreed. We'll send the architecture doc and a network checklist. Diego, can you run the deep-dive with Liam next week?
[05:48] Diego: Yep, I'm available. I'll propose times for 2026-07-07.
[05:52] Liam: That works.
[05:54] Priya: Also please include examples for PrivateLink endpoint configuration and endpoint policy samples — we have an internal security gate that reviews templates.
[06:02] Diego: Will do — I'll include a sample endpoint policy, example route table entries, and a CloudFormation snippet for the VPC endpoints.
[06:10] Asha: Any blockers on our side for demoing the workload? We might need an NDA for access to certain docs.
[06:16] Maya: We can get the NDA in motion; security pack will go out after.
[06:21] Asha: Cool. One minor transcription note: sometimes I see reference to 'K-V cash' in old docs — that's KV cache, right?
[06:28] Diego: Yes, KV cache — key/value cache for transformer context, not a financial thing.
[06:32] Maya: (laughs) Not a bank.
[06:35] Diego: Quick callouts: If you want minimal network changes, PrivateLink is the easiest. If you need absolute lowest latency and bulk throughput, peering/TGW or running in your account is best. We'll enumerate pros/cons in the doc.
[06:48] Asha: Sounds good. Anything else?
[06:51] Priya: One more — data residency: can metadata or logs be excluded from leaving region? We need all logs to stay in us-east-1.
[06:59] Diego: Yes, we can configure log export targets in-region; for Private deployments we ensure data plane locality per your config. We'll confirm in the architecture doc.
[07:09] Maya: Great — recap of immediate next steps: I'll send security pack, SOC2/ISO under NDA, and pricing. Diego will send network checklist and sample CF/Terraform and schedule deep-dive with Liam for 2026-07-07. Liam will share VPC ranges and NAT/proxy details.
[07:26] Asha: Thanks, everyone. Look forward to the docs.
[07:29] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up. Bye.

End of transcript.
